title: Close a stand-mounted micrometer on a 20 mm gauge block with its ratchet and lock it
instruction: Put the gauge block between the micrometer's faces, close the spindle on it with the ratchet knob until it clicks three times, and set the lock lever. Do not use the thimble to squeeze the block.
context: Inspectors, testers, sorters, samplers, and weighers (SOC 51-9061, about 0.6 million US jobs, BLS) check parts with outside micrometers, and check the micrometers themselves on gauge blocks. The spindle is run up by the thimble and finished only by the ratchet knob, which slips at a set torque so every reading is taken at the same light force: two or three clicks, then lock. A part squeezed with the thimble reads small, wears the faces and gives a different number to the next inspector. The lock holds the reading while the part is taken out. On a bench stand the part is slid in along the work plate against the frame, so the stand and the frame are part of the job.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is z = 0. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up; arm bases at y +30.5 cm and -30.5 cm. Two objects. (1) Micrometer on its bench stand, fixed. Stand: a steel base 185 x 90 x 30 mm (x 150 to 335 mm, y -45 to +45 mm); its top is the work plate, 30 mm up, lapped flush with the anvil face (a 6.35 mm carbide disc at x 240 mm, y 0). Two steel guide rails, 4 mm wide and 2.5 mm tall, run along x on the plate from x 219.5 to 335 mm at y +-7.25 mm (a 10.5 mm channel). Behind the axis a rear post (20 x 36 mm, 45 mm tall) with a clamp jaw (10 x 32 mm, 20 mm tall) and a black clamp-screw knob (14 mm across) holds the frame's column. Micrometer: an outside micrometer of the 0 to 25 mm class (Mitutoyo 103-137 class, 0.01 mm graduation, 0.5 mm of spindle travel per thimble turn), upright, anvil down. Its blue steel C-frame has a column (20 x 26 mm, 29 mm tall, x 199.5 to 219.5 mm) with black insulating pads on its flanks, and an arm forward to the spindle's boss over the axis (underside 23.3 mm over the plate): the C is open toward the robot and the column's front face is 20.5 mm behind the axis. The spindle (6.35 mm carbide face) starts open to 20.30 mm over the plate. Above the frame: a lock collar 19 mm across with a red lock lever 30 x 8 x 5 mm lying along +y (it flips 90 degrees clockwise seen from above, to point at +x, about 0.5 N at its tip); the thimble, silver, 20 mm across, 19.5 mm long, 35 to 54.5 mm over the plate; the ratchet knob, black, 18 mm across, 12 mm long, 54.8 to 66.8 mm over the plate. Each has a thin index line. From as found, 216 degrees of clockwise thimble turn (seen from above) bring the faces onto a 20.000 mm block; the knob then clicks every 15 degrees of slip. (2) Gauge block, loose: grade 0 steel, 20.000 mm between its measuring faces, 35 x 9 mm faces, 49.5 g, friction 0.2, standing on a 35 x 9 mm face in the rails' channel with its long side along x, centred at x 295 mm, y 0 (55 mm in front of the axis; front end at x 312.5 mm), its measuring faces horizontal. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: End state plus a log of the whole run, from the micrometer's joints and the block's pose. Gap: the distance between the two faces at the last step. Between faces: the block's centre within 14.3 mm of the axis along x and 1.3 mm along y (each 6.35 mm face wholly on a 35 x 9 mm face), standing on the plate (centre 10 mm up, within 1.5 mm), its measuring faces within 5 degrees of square to the spindle. Touch: between faces with the gap 20.02 mm or less. Clicks: each 15 degrees the ratchet knob slips on the thimble counts one click (the most it reached), but only while the faces are seated on the block (touch, and the thimble within 2 degrees of its 216 degree touch turn) and the lock lever is off (under 34 degrees); slip on a locked spindle, or with the faces short of the block, earns none. Locked: the lever turned 80 degrees or more. Squeezed: at any step with the block between the faces, the thimble turned more than 10 degrees past the 216 degrees at which the faces touch it (about 14 N at 1 N per micron, est). Fell: at any step the block's centre more than 5 mm below the plate's top. Hands off: on every step of the last 1 s both grippers' finger zones are 30 mm or more from the block, spindle, thimble, ratchet knob and lever, and over that 1 s the block moves under 0.5 mm and turns under 1 degree and the thimble, knob and lever turn under 1 degree. Score 0 if squeezed or fell, and 0 unless hands off. Otherwise: 1.0 between faces, gap within 0.03 mm of 20.000, 3 or more clicks, locked; 0.75 the same, not locked; 0.5 between faces, gap within 0.03 mm, 1 or 2 clicks; 0.25 between faces, gap within 0.20 mm of 20.000, otherwise; 0 in every other case, including a run that ends with no block between the faces. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0. Success: 1.0 held for 1 s. Real trial, per condition: gap, the scale to 0.01 mm; between faces, a look from above with a 5 degree gauge and a 1.3 mm feeler; clicks, by ear with the knob marked in 15 degree steps, counted only with the lever off and the scale at 20.00; locked, the lever against an 80 degree mark; squeezed, a line scribed across thimble and barrel at the first click, and the thimble must not pass a 10 degree mark (or a 50 N load button under the block peaks under 14 N); fell, a rule 5 mm below the plate; hands off, a 30 mm spacer, video, and a dial indicator on the thimble's rim (1 degree is 0.17 mm).
reset_notes: Open the spindle to 20.30 mm on the scale, with the lock lever off (pointing +y). Stand the gauge block in the rails' channel with its long side along x, centred at x 295 mm, y 0, the front end toward the robot. Wipe the faces and the block with a clean cloth between trials. Nothing is consumed; check the micrometer's zero on its closed setting once a day.
fidelity: Rigid bodies. Declared rules, applied every control step: the screw (the spindle is driven to 0.5 mm per thimble turn and stopped at the block); the ratchet (the knob turns the thimble until the faces touch the block, then slips, one click per 15 degrees; its torque limit is not modelled); the lever's two-notch cam. The squeeze is the thimble's turn past touch at an estimated 1 N per micron. Thimble travel along the barrel (0.3 mm) is not drawn. Friction 0.2 (est).
